_status: DRAFT — NOT INSTALLABLE. Deliberately kept out of packs/ and index.json.
_why: This pack's rules are opa/Rego and reference input.event.provider_account_email, which the agent's own event schema already carries (agent/internal/events/types.go, EventRecord.ProviderAccountEmail, populated on KindSessionStart for tools with a reliably-available local signal -- see agent/internal/sources/provideraccount) but which is NOT currently exposed to Rego policy evaluation. Both Rego input builders would need the same one-line addition: agent/internal/policy/opa/rule.go's buildRegoInput() and agent/internal/policy/opa/engine.go's regoInput() -- CLAUDE.md's 'two orchestrators' warning applies here too; a fix to only one leaves the other scenario silently evaluating against an empty string. Until that lands, every rule below always evaluates false (the config's approved_domains check never fires, and personal_account never matches) -- installing this pack today would create a policy group that looks active but never fires, which is worse than not installing it at all.
_verified: The Rego in both rules below was actually compiled AND evaluated (not just hand-written), via a throwaway scratch package under agent/cmd/ that was deleted immediately after -- 7 cases covering fire/no-fire/edge cases (empty allowlist, missing email signal, non-session_start event) all passed. Caught my own mistake in the process: agent/internal/policy/opa/rule.go imports the OLD `github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/rego` path (not `.../opa/v1/rego`), which parses Rego in v0 mode by default -- an `if`-keyword v1-style first draft of this Rego compiled fine against the newer `/v1/rego` import but FAILED against the actual import this codebase uses (`rego_parse_error: var cannot be used for rule name`). The Rego below is the corrected v0-style version (`match { ... }`, no `if`, `=` for assignment, `arr[_]` indexing) verified against the real import path -- matches agent/internal/policy/opa/rule_test.go's own existing example style.
name: Non-Corporate Accounts Baseline (DRAFT)
description: Flags sessions authenticated with a personal AI-provider account, or an email domain outside an approved allowlist. Mirrors the competitor's 2-rule 'Non-Corporate Accounts' category. Both rules use the opa rule_type since this is genuinely session/identity-scoped, not content/command-scoped -- no existing non-Rego rule_type can express it, but no NEW rule_type is needed either, since opa/Rego can already reference input.config (the rule_config below) and would be able to reference input.event.provider_account_email once that field is wired in.

rules.name: Require justification for personal AI-provider accounts
rules.description: Flags a session_start event whose provider_account_email domain matches a known personal-email-provider domain (gmail.com, outlook.com, hotmail.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, protonmail.com, aol.com -- adjust via rule_config.personal_domains). Requires a written reason before the session's activity is treated as trusted.

rule_config.rego:
package tracelet.agent

domain_parts = split(input.event.provider_account_email, "@")

match {
	input.event.normalized_kind == "session_start"
	input.event.provider_account_email != ""
	count(domain_parts) == 2
	domain_parts[1] == input.config.personal_domains[_]
}

rules.name: Require justification for AI-provider accounts outside the approved domain list
rules.description: Flags a session_start event whose provider_account_email domain is NOT in rule_config.approved_domains. Until at least one domain is configured, this rule cannot fire (an empty allow-list means nothing is 'outside' it) -- mirrors the competitor's own stated behaviour for this rule. Requires a written reason before the session's activity is treated as trusted.
